messages.subject: -Inf in FIRMA score matrix
parts:
Hi all,

I ran a FIRMA on a data set consisting of 179 Affymetrix Human Exon
Arrays and after checking the results, I discovered that each and
every probeset has at least one -Inf entry in the scores matrix. It
sticks out that the score for one specific array is -Inf for every
probeset, although the corresponding values after RMA are in the
normal range and finite. Moreover, some of the probesets have two -Inf
entries while the others do not.
I performed LIMMA and MiDAS to check whether problems occur with the
data set, but both work fine on the RMA values. Additionally, I ran
the same script on another data set with less samples before and there
were no such problems.
Hence at this point I'm not sure how to go on processing the data...
You can find the code example below, any help or remarks are greatly
appreciated.

Best regards and thank you in advance,
René


######
# RMA

chipType = "HuEx-1_0-st-v2"
verbose = Arguments$getVerbose(-8, timestamp=TRUE)
cdf = AffymetrixCdfFile$byChipType(chipType,
tags=paste(level,"R3,A20071112,EP",sep=""))
cs = AffymetrixCelSet$byName(dataset, cdf=cdf)
setCdf(cs, cdf)
bc = RmaBackgroundCorrection(cs, tag=paste(level,"R3",sep=""))
csBC = process(bc,verbose=verbose)
qn = QuantileNormalization(csBC, typesToUpdate="pm")
csN = process(qn, verbose=verbose)

plmTr = ExonRmaPlm(csN, mergeGroups=TRUE)
fit(plmTr, verbose=verbose)
cesTr = getChipEffectSet(plmTr)
trFit = extractDataFrame(cesTr, units=NULL, addNames=TRUE)

plmEx = ExonRmaPlm(csN, mergeGroups=FALSE)
fit(plmEx, verbose=verbose)
cesEx = getChipEffectSet(plmEx)
ExFit = extractDataFrame(cesEx, units=NULL, addNames=TRUE)

######
# FIRMA

firma = FirmaModel(plmTr)
fit(firma, verbose=verbose)
fs = getFirmaScores(firma)
fsScores = extractDataFrame(fs)
fsScores = cbind(ExprMatrix[,1:5],log2(fsScores[,-c(1:3)]))

messages.author: 185f4d4fdb048fb8
messages.subject: Re: [aroma.affymetrix] -Inf in FIRMA score matrix
parts:
Hi.

The FIRMA scores are calculated as the *median* of the PLM residuals
(divided by an estimate of the std dev), cf. Eqn for F_ij (page 3) in
the Purdom et al. (2008) paper. Thus, in order to achieve F_ij =
-Inf, at least have of the PLM residuals (on the log scale) must be
-Inf. On the non-log scale, this corresponds to having zeros.

You can retrieve the residuals used via:

rs <- calculateResiduals(plmTr);

# E.g. look at the (non-logged) residuals for unit/transcript #4305:
eps <- readUnits(rs, units=4305);
print(eps);

Do you see those zeros?

/Henrik
